digest.component_or_area: code review LLM framework / CI gate compatibility verifier
propositions: Newly added hard-fail CI gates/steps without if-present/grandfather guards break branches created before the gate was added, causing regressions in in-flight branches.

Code review criterion project.ci-gate-compat must declare pipeline-config file patterns (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, Bitbucket, Drone) via a declarative applies_to glob seam to trigger only on pipeline changes, not via hard-coded vendor-specific Python code paths.

The applies_to glob set for project.ci-gate-compat must be project-overridable via [code_review] ci_config_globs config key, where a non-empty list replaces the shipped globs, allowing unusual pipelines to be declared without enumerating all CI vendors in the core package.

Changed files matching any applied glob must select project.ci-gate-compat for dispatch; changed files matching no globs must drop the criterion, while project.review-phase-boundaries (empty applies_to) remains always-on.

The rubric must ask a CI-agnostic question about hard-fail/grandfather semantics without naming GitHub, Jenkins, GitLab, CircleCI, Buildkite, Bitbucket, or Drone, so the criterion remains portable across CI systems.

The criterion ships as advisory (default_posture: advisory, blocking_enabled: false, block_threshold: 0.90) with a balanced 6/6 fire/pass evaluation corpus (CG-F1–F6, CG-N1–N6) and zero deployment-blocking verdict until calibration on real reviews.
